Gort the Skullcrusher

Overview

Gort the Skullcrusher commands the village warriors and supports Erfar’s use of the Chosen legend. He pressures Zak into fighting goblins and supplies information about the stolen bridge mechanism. When accused of treachery, he openly declares his ambition to become the village’s ruler and threatens to return with the forest men. [1, 2, 3, 4]

The village and the Chosen

At the village assembly, Erfar the Silvertongue identifies Zak with the promised Chosen who was to appear at the Sacred Ruins. Gort the Skullcrusher, the captain, supports the ceremony. The offer of food, shelter and honour comes with a threat: an impostor would be thrown into the fire. Zak accepts the title and gives his name. Erfar immediately sends him against the goblin sentry watching the village, reasoning that his plain clothes and unusual metal knife will let him approach where armed villagers cannot. Afterwards Zak learns that this is Gipath’s only human village, with no king or known route to other lands. [1, 5, 6, 7]

The wolf, the captain and the craftsman

Killing the sentry brings another request from Erfar: the White Wolf and its pack are taking the village livestock. After Zak kills their leader, Erfar and Gort press him to surrender the head so the captain can claim prestige. Gort also sends him to punish the goblins while the village soldiers stay home. Meanwhile Babur the Tightfist refuses to work until his stolen iron tools are returned. Erfar calls the thieves friendly “Free Hunters”; Babur calls them brigands and describes the beating of his apprentice. Recovering the chisel and bodkin from the chief and his wife wins Zak the craftsman’s services. These early errands expose the disagreement between the village’s leaders and the man who equips it. [8, 9, 10, 2, 11, 12, 13, 14]

The brigands’ trail and the Magic Bit

Babur’s account of a red-haired brigand meeting orcs gives Zak his next lead. A map taken from Redhead points to a Magic Bit in a sarcophagus in the orc cave. Babur explains that Estera values such objects, while Gort can supply the missing drawbridge mechanism. Zak obtains the seer’s key and the object, then asks how to reach the witch. Babur, who made her spare trap key, explains the guarded ravines and controlling obelisks. The craftsman expects a share of the sale. Zak instead intends to exchange the find for help with his lost memory. [13, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21]

The supposed attack on the goblins

While Zak seeks the magician, Erfar and Gort arrange another joint operation with the Free Hunters, supposedly to prevent a goblin raid. The promised friendly meeting becomes an ambush by brigands and village soldiers. Erfar denies responsibility, while Babur warns that the elder is trying to have Zak killed. A note in the newer orc script cannot yet settle the matter: Estera needs an Orc ABC Book to read it. Its translation reveals a contract on Zak’s life, a detailed description of him and a substantial payment. The search for the author becomes a separate investigation alongside the route into the Dead City. [22, 23, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28]

Gort’s rebellion

The written instructions to kill Zak expose Gort’s handwriting. Confronted with the evidence, the captain turns against the authority he formerly served and declares that he will rule the village himself. He flees to gather the forest men. Erfar urges Zak to stop him before he can return; the ensuing pursuit ends Gort’s rebellion. Rivar the Hulk becomes the new captain. Unlike his predecessor, Rivar admits that he dislikes fighting, shares his family’s secret of strength and later supports Zak when suspicion finally reaches the elder. [29, 4, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35]
